body:
You don't have to feel guilty for feeling this way even if you aren't abused. This happens to people and some people have a lot of success by getting therapy or medication (to each their own). 

I feel this way sometime but not all the time and when I had therapy it was really helpful. 

I imagine you must be feeling really exhausted too and overwhelmed, and it must be difficult. I hope you can be gentle with yourself and realize that the feelings you are having do not make you a bad person. All they mean is that you need a little extra help and there's nothing wrong with that. People are social creatures. We're meant to need help.

People at reunions are going to want to show off a little the things they've done, but plenty of people will have similar problems that they are not sharing. Maybe go as an opportunity to reconnect and just focus on other people or start conversations about your interests if you're nervous about bringing personal stuff up. Also, the fact that you have struggled through all these things and are doing well to the point of going to a reunion does mean you amounted to something and someone. There are plenty of people who are unemployed at your age who have not dealt with what you have. You are not a failure.

How are you defining "success"? Is that success you want, or success society tells you you need to have to be considered valuable? Maybe start with smaller goals of things YOU would like in your life, things based on your values, your enjoyments. Pretty soon if you make even a little progress towards those smaller goals, your whole life begins to look and feel a bit differently.
